paragraphs: Onigiri are Japanese rice balls rather than sushi: plain warm short-grain rice is shaped with lightly salted hands around compact fillings and often wrapped in nori just before eating.

Onigiri is not sushi: the rice is plain, warm short-grain rice seasoned through lightly salted hands rather than vinegar. Salmon is cooked firmer and saltier than a dinner fillet so the compact filling seasons the surrounding rice. This Kwilt version follows the reviewed household adaptation: Use a centered salmon filling rather than mixing it through every grain, preserving plain-rice contrast and making seasoning obvious in each bite.

heroImage.altText: Japanese salmon onigiri shaped into neat triangles with plain short-grain rice, salted roasted salmon filling, sesame, and crisp nori strips.
